rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE DOWNSTREAM PETROLEUM INDUSTRY AND FOR OTHER RELATED PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Contends that there is a pressing need to regulate the oil industry to protect the majority of Filipinos from current runaway increases in oil prices and assumes that regulation can only be effective and truly beneficial if it is part of a program to institutionalize national oil industrialization, so that local oil prices can be brought down from unreasonable and unjustifiable levels and can be prevented from falling prey to further monopoly pricing and manipulation.

Intends therefore the regulation of the petroleum industry through the creation of an independent, quasi-judicial regulatory body to be named  as Petroleum Regulatory Council (PRC); and a trust	                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      fund  which shall be designated as the Oil Price Buffer Fund (OPBF)  which shall serve to cushion the impact on consumers against drastic increases in petroleum prices.
rows.status: Substituted by HB10823

rows.author: I083
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING CENTRALIZED PROCUREMENT OF PETROLEUM IN THE COUNTRY
rows.abstract:
Declares that the act and business of importing, exporting, re-exporting, distributing, and selling at wholesale of crude oil, gasoline, kerosene, gas, and other refined petroleum products, as well as operations and activities of natural and juridical persons, firms, and entities engaged in the petroleum industry shall be carried out in a manner consistent with the public interest.

Highlights the objectives and purposes of the bill as regards to:  indigenous petroleum and petroleum-based resources, primarily for the general welfare; proper, adequate, and continuous supply of crude oil and refined petroleum products; reasonable prices for petroleum products and to prevent monopoly, combinations in restraint of trade, unfair competition, and economic dominations; and minimal cost and outflow of foreign exchange involved in the operations of the industry.

Creates the Philippine National Oil Company-National Petroleum Exchange Corporation (PNOC-NPEC); Renationalizes the Petron Corporation and repeals R.A. 8479, also known as the “Downstream Oil Industry Deregulations Act of 1998”.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2019-09-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE BUREAU OF JAIL MANAGEMENT AND PENOLOGY TO EXERCISE SUPERVISION AND CONTROL OVER PROVINCIAL JAILS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Proposes to establish a national standard in the operational management of all jails in the country to attain uniformity and greater efficiency in the implementation of the plans and programs geared towards the effective rehabilitation of inmates.

States that each provincial jail shall be headed by a provincial jail warden with a rank of superintendent, who must be a graduate of bachelor of laws or a holder of a master´s degree in management, public administration, public safety, criminology, penology, sociology, national security administration, defense studies or other related disciplines from a recognized institution of learning, and must have satisfactorily passed the necessary or career courses for such position

rows.title_full: AN ACT FURTHER AMENDING ARTICLES 29, 97, 98 AND 99 OF ACT NO. 3815, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE
rows.abstract:
Proposes to amend the Good Conduct Time Allowance (GCTA) Law in order to put a stop to whatever
grave abuse of discretion in its implementation which is contrary to the good intention impelled 
by the reformatory or rehabilitative spirit of the modern penal system, rather than by purely 
punitive nature.

Provides for other exemptions of cases as enumerated hereunder, when the offenders or accused who have undergone preventive imprisonment shall be credited in the service of their sentence consisting 
of deprivation of liberty, with the full time during which they have undergone preventive imprisonment:
a.) when they are habitual delinquents; b.) when they are escapees; and 3.) when they have been 
charged with and convicted of heinous crimes as specified in this Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2019-09-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING GOOD MANNERS AND RIGHT CONDUCT (GMRC) IN THE K-12 CURRICULUM
rows.abstract:
Intends to restore GMRC/Values Education as a separate subject in the present K-12 program in basic
education curriculum - focusing on the character development and moral values formation of students relating to self, to the community, to the country, to the environment, and to God which shall include theoretical, practical, and biblical principles in its enforcement to all students.

States that the mother tongue of the majority of the learners shall be adopted as the primary medium 
of instruction for teaching this subject and provides for corresponding number of hours required per 
school year for Elementary (60 hours); Junior High School (80 hours); and Senior High School (100 hours).

rows.title_full: COLLECTIVE INVESTMENT SCHEMES LAW
rows.abstract:
States that a Collective Investment Scheme is any arrangement whereby funds are solicited from the investing public and pooled together for the purpose of investing, re-investing and/or trading in securities or other investment assets or different classes thereof as allowed under this Law.

Aims to establish a comprehensive regulatory and tax framework to enable CIS and all the participants
therein to play a key role in the development of the capital market through the promotion of investor protection and growth of pooled investments and capital development; encourage participation of the best qualified fund managers/investment advisers; broaden participation by Filipinos in ownership of securities/other investment  assets; equal protection to investors in all similar CIS, imposing same requirements and providing same competitive environment; and responsible investing through the dissemination of information on the opportunities and risks involved.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT 7103, \"OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE IRON AND STEEL INDUSTRY ACT\", PROVIDING FOR STIFFER PENALTIES AND SANCTIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract:
Seeks to provide stiffer penalties for smuggling of iron and steel products and provide a set of quality and industry standards for iron and steel products.

Declares that upon the operation of the smelting plants, penalties shall be imposed upon any person who shall smuggle, fraudulently import or bring goods into the Philippines that constitute the intermediate or final product of the manufacturing activity described in Sec.5(b) of this Act, or who shall receive, conceal, buy or in a manner facilitate the transportation, concealment, or sale after importation of such products.

rows.author: J113
rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPOSING THE DEATH PENALTY ON CERTAIN HEINOUS CRIMES, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9346, ENTITLED \"AN ACT PROHIBITING THE IMPOSITION OF DEATH PENALTY IN THE PHILIPPINES\" AND AMENDING ACT NO. 3815, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE \"REVISED PENAL CODE,\" AND OTHER SPECIAL PENAL LAWS
rows.abstract:
Proposes to restore the death sentence in the country by imposing the penalty on heinous crimes as defined under Act No.3815, as amended such as treason; qualified piracy; qualified bribery; parricide; murder; infanticide; rape; kidnapping and serious illegal detention; robbery with violence against or intimidation of persons; destructive arson; plunder; carnapping; and illegal acts/activities related to dangerous drugs and/or controlled precursors and essential chemical.

States that the death penalty shall not be imposed when the guilty person is below eighteen years of age when the crime was committed or is more that seventy years of age when upon appeal or automatic review of the case by the Supreme Courts, the required majority vote is not obtained for said imposition.

Declares that the death sentence shall be executed with preference to any other penalty and shall
consist in putting the person under the sentence to death by either hanging, firing squad or
lethal injection.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2019-09-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING THE MAGNA CARTA NG PILIPINONG MARINO
rows.abstract:
Contends that existing labor laws and legislation, especially the Overseas Filipinos and Migrant Worker's Act,  do not adhere to the adopted Maritime Labor Convention of 2006 (also known as the \"Seafarer's Bill of Rights\"), which was designed to be applicable internationally and ensure minimum standards for the safe and secure workplace that complies with safety standards and other forms of social protection.

Intends to fill the gaps in legislation and comply and effectively implement the standards set by the international convention to promote the welfare and protect the rights of Filipino seafarers.

Tasks the Philippine Seafarer One Stop Processing Center (PSOC) to operationalize and make available to the public, an integrated document processing center for the seafarers and the general public to conduct official transactions.

rows.author: I054
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE WARNING, ALERT, AND RESPONSE NETWORK 911 ACT OF 2016 OR THE \"WARN 911\" AS THE NATIONWIDE EMERGENCY HOTLINE NUMBER AND PROVIDING PENALTY TO PRANK CALLS THEREOF
rows.abstract:
Proposes to institutionalize the WARN hotline 911 Public Safety Answering Center (Call Center) in
every Region, Province, City, Municipality and Barangay and identifies its major service
responders such as: PNP, BFP, BJMP, PCG, PDEA, NBI, MMDA, PNRC, BSP, EARnet (Emergency Assistance and Response Network, Volunteer NGOs, affiliated civic sector groups, and other affiliated public safety volunteers.

Seeks also to institutionalize: the WARN 911 Community-Based Volunteer Network constituting Volunteer Service Responders Network; and the WARN 911 Development Office where existing DILG PATROL \"117\" Development Group activated by the DILG under the PATROL \"117\" Commission is tasks to implement the WARN 911 Program.

Declares that the WARN 911 Development Office shall coordinate with the NDRRMC and the corresponding LDRRMCs to address, prevent and mitigate a potential or existing disasters in the community; and guarantees the non-applicability of Republic Act No.4200 or the Anti-Wiretapping Act to a call made to WARN 911.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2019-09-25

rows.author: I040
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE COMMUNITY-DRIVEN DEVELOPMENT APPROACH AS A NATIONAL STRATEGY FOR INCLUSIVE GROWTH AND SOCIAL PROTECTION, MANDATING ALL NATIONAL GOVERNMENT AGENCIES AND DEPARTMENTS, INCLUDING THEIR ATTACHED AGENCIES, OFFICES AND BUREAUS, LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS, AND OTHER GOVERNMENT INSTRUMENTALITIES TO IMPLEMENT THEIR COMMUNITY-BASED PROGRAMS, ACTIVITIES, AND PROJECTS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Seeks to address the lack of an enabling policy, a national strategy and its mechanisms for
community empowerment, by enhancing capacities for community participation, especially the
poor, vulnerable, disadvantaged, and marginalized in the local development process.

Intends to reinforce the value of participatory governance by complementing the LGC which
mandates LGUs, among others, to provide basic services to constituents; and offers a step-by-
step process and ready technologies that were all proven effective in stirring lasting active citizenship and allows even residents who are not part of organizations to have a voice.

Institutionalizes the Kalahi-CIDSS (Kapit-Bisig Laban sa Kahirapan Comprehensive and Integrated
Delivery of Social Services) as a Community Driven Development program; and Creates an Inter-Agency 
Advisory Council on CDD Institutionalization and the CDD Knowledge and Resource Institute (CDD KRI).
rows.status: Transmitted to the Committee on Appropriations on 2021-02-16

rows.author: J095
rows.title_full: AN ACT SETTING MINIMUM STANDARDS FOR THE OPERATION OF INTERNET CAFES
rows.abstract:
Mandates all Local Government Units to enforce the provisions of this Act and all similar establishments
shall be covered under this Act.

Specifies adequate facilities for establishments offering computer services such as:
a) system, program, or application which can aid the monitoring of the time spent by each client;
b) sufficient ventilation, or if needed, an airconditioning;
c) regularly cleaned comfort room/lavatory with a closed-flush toilet.

Requires other regulations such as: a) a computer may be rented for only six (6) hours per person in
one session; b) students in basic/secondary education shall not be allowed to rent a computer to play
games from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. during weekdays, excluding holidays/other special observances

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE NATIONAL FINANCIAL LITERACY COUNCIL AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Intends to address Filipinos' lack of financial literacy or capability in managing their day-to-day finances, as well as their access to formal financial institutions (banks, insurance and investment companies) that would aid them to acquire specific knowledge to make informed financial decisions.

Seeks to instill financial literacy in young Filipino by incorporating its modules to the basic education
system which shall include budgeting, financial basics such as the effect of compound interest in debt,
savings, and investments, and time value of money.
             
Aims to: integrate financial literacy in the implementation of poverty alleviation; promote financial literacy in all government and private workplaces; and disseminate financial education materials through various media platforms.
rows.status: Substituted by HB07701
